record.context_brief: same continuous spectrum but different metric type
record.original_question: Do there exist metrically non-isomorphic measure-preserving dynamical systems that nevertheless have the same continuous spectrum, in particular the same Lebesgue spectrum?

evidence.quote: Предлагаемая работа возникла из попыток автора решить известную спектральную проблему теории динамических систем: существуют ли метрически различные динамические системы с одним и тем же непрерывным (в частности, лебеговским) спектром?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation. The associated Koopman operator $U_T$ on $L^2_0(X,\mu)=\{f\in L^2(X,\mu):\int f\,d\mu=0\}$ is the unitary operator defined by $U_T f = f\circ T$. The maximal spectral type of $T$ is the equivalence class of measures on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$ given by the spectral theorem applied to $U_T$, together with its multiplicity function. The transformation $T$ is said to have continuous spectrum if its maximal spectral type (restricted to $L^2_0$) is a continuous (non-atomic) measure on $\mathbb{T}$, and to have Lebesgue spectrum if this maximal spectral type is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{T}$. Two measure-preserving systems $(X_1,\mu_1,T_1)$ and $(X_2,\mu_2,T_2)$ are metrically isomorphic if there exists a measure-preserving bijection (mod null sets) $\phi:X_1\to X_2$ with $\phi\circ T_1=T_2\circ\phi$ a.e.

Question: Do there exist two measure-preserving dynamical systems that are not metrically isomorphic but whose Koopman operators on $L^2_0$ have the same spectral invariants (maximal spectral type and multiplicity function), in particular both having Lebesgue spectrum (of the same multiplicity)?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of metrically non-isomorphic measure-preserving systems with the same continuous spectrum is classically known: Anzai gave the first example of non-isomorphic automorphisms with the same spectrum, and Kolmogorov–Ornstein theory shows that all Bernoulli shifts have countable Lebesgue spectrum yet are classified up to isomorphism by entropy, providing a continuum of non-isomorphic systems sharing the same (countable) Lebesgue spectrum. Refinements (e.g., constructions giving continua of spectrally nonisomorphic transformations with even-multiplicity Lebesgue components, and the affirmative resolution of Banach's problem on simple Lebesgue spectrum in the σ-finite setting) further confirm that the spectrum is far from a complete metric invariant.

status_evidence.title: Spectral theory of dynamical systems (Kanigowski–Lemańczyk survey)
status_evidence.snippet: The first example of a pair of non-isomorphic automorphisms with the same spectrum was proposed by Anzai; systems with Lebesgue spectrum need not be spatially isomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: Non-isomorphic systems with the same (Lebesgue) spectrum are known to exist.

status_evidence.title: Ergodic Banach problem, flat polynomials and Mahler's measures
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a continuum of spectrally nonisomorphic transformations with even-multiplicity Lebesgue component; affirmative answer to Banach's problem on simple Lebesgue spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Many non-isomorphic systems sharing Lebesgue-type spectra have been constructed.
